diagnosis: The checks C1, C2, and C3 passed because the lone decision-maker assigned the exact personnel based on the shared public facts PF1, PF2, and PF3, respectively. These assignments were directly linked to the decisive facts that the lone decision-maker never had access to, namely PF1, PF2, and PF3. This indicates a structural leak where the model can infer the correct assignments without needing the hidden information.

C1.why: The current host-nation language qualification changes the partner-liaison assignment from an uninformed choice among the three personnel to the exact choice of Sgt Malik.

C2.why: The current POL and hazardous-material accountability certification changes the POL-accountability assignment to the exact choice of Cpl Ortiz.

C3.why: The current movement-control-system operator certification changes the movement-control assignment to the exact choice of Spc Vega.

fix_instructions: Tighten checks C1, C2, and C3 to require the hidden information contained in PF1, PF2, and PF3. Specifically, modify check C1 to require the decision-maker to choose 'Sgt Malik' as the partner liaison if and only if the current host-nation language qualification applies. Similarly, modify check C2 to require the decision-maker to assign 'Cpl Ortiz' as the POL accountability officer if and only if the current POL and hazardous-material accountability certification applies. Finally, modify check C3 to require the decision-maker to assign 'Spc Vega' as the movement control officer if and only if the current movement-control-system operator certification applies.
